rationale: The assistant gave safe, correctly isolated homeowner checks (impeller inspection with filter out, Drain/Spin test after a stall) and respected the customer's refusal to remove panels, keeping pump and level-sensing both in play without naming a part. However it never asked whether a light-flash pattern or error code appears when the machine stalls, never asked for the full model number, and did not clearly recommend an engineer for what is an intermittent fault that the ground truth says needs professional diagnosis; it also leaned toward 'an intermittent drain pump is currently the leading possibility' while ignoring a possible control fault. The third reply largely restated the Drain/Spin interpretation from the first. Useful but unfinished progress with no safety or fabrication failures.
